lit: when the water rises, the boat rises with it

use.how: Predicate, often after 也 or 跟着: one thing goes up because what it depends on went up. 房价涨了，房租也水涨船高。

near.diff: 蒸蒸日上 praises steady, thriving growth of its own; 水涨船高 says something rises only because its base or surroundings rose.

cue: House prices in the area jumped, and within months every landlord nearby had raised the rent too. How do you describe the rents?

ctx.s: 房价涨了，附近的房租也跟着{水涨船高}。
ctx.en: House prices went up, and rents nearby rose right along with them.

ctx.s: 他拿了冠军以后，出场费{水涨船高}。
ctx.en: After he won the championship, his appearance fee went up accordingly.

ctx.s: “这家店的菜怎么又贵了？”“肉价涨了，菜价自然{水涨船高}。”
ctx.en: "Why has this restaurant put its prices up again?" "Meat got dearer, so naturally the dishes did too."

ctx.s: 大家的整体水平提高了，比赛的难度也{水涨船高}。
ctx.en: Everyone's overall level has improved, so the competitions have become harder as well.

ctx.s: 随着城市的发展，这一带的地价{水涨船高}，老居民纷纷卖了房子。
ctx.en: As the city grew, land prices here climbed with it, and the old residents sold up one after another.

ctx.s: 公司业绩越来越好，员工的待遇也{水涨船高}。
ctx.en: The company kept doing better, and the staff's pay and benefits rose along with it.

bad.s: 经济不景气，大家的工资都{水涨船高}，越来越少了。
bad.en: (meant: the economy is bad and everyone's pay keeps shrinking)
bad.why: It only describes something going up with its surroundings; it cannot describe a fall.

bad.s: 老板决定{水涨船高}我们的工资。
bad.en: (meant: the boss decided to raise our pay)
bad.why: It is not a transitive verb meaning 'to raise'; it describes a rise that follows from something else rising.

mean: to drift with the current, having no views of one's own
lit: to follow the waves and chase the current

use.how: Predicate or after 不愿/不能: criticises someone who just goes along with the crowd or circumstances. 他不想随波逐流。

near.diff: 入乡随俗 is sensibly adopting local customs, a good thing; 随波逐流 is having no direction of one's own and letting others decide.
人云亦云 is repeating what others say; 随波逐流 is the broader habit of going wherever the crowd or the times push you.

cue: Everyone in her class chose finance because it pays well, but she wanted to study art and refused to just follow them. What did she refuse to do?

ctx.s: 做人要有自己的想法，不能{随波逐流}。
ctx.en: You need ideas of your own; you can't just drift along with everyone else.

ctx.s: 同学们都去学金融，她却不愿{随波逐流}，选了美术。
ctx.en: Her classmates all went into finance, but she refused to follow the crowd and chose art.

ctx.s: “你为什么也买这个？”“大家都买，我就{随波逐流}了。”
ctx.en: "Why did you buy one too?" "Everyone was buying it, so I just went along with it."

ctx.s: 这几年他一直{随波逐流}，到现在还不知道自己想做什么。
ctx.en: For years he has just drifted along, and he still doesn't know what he wants to do.

ctx.s: 市场上流行什么，这家工厂就生产什么，一味{随波逐流}，始终没有自己的品牌。
ctx.en: The factory makes whatever happens to be in fashion, always just following the market, and has never built a brand of its own.

ctx.s: 这位作家始终坚持自己的风格，从不{随波逐流}。
ctx.en: This writer has always kept her own style and never just gone along with the trend.

bad.s: 他到了国外很快就{随波逐流}，适应得特别好。
bad.en: (meant: abroad he quickly adapted to local ways and settled in well)
bad.why: It criticises having no views of one's own; sensibly adapting to a new place calls for a different idiom, about following local customs.

bad.s: 我决定{随波逐流}大家的意见。
bad.en: (meant: I decided to go along with everyone's opinion)
bad.why: It takes no object: the person who drifts is the subject, and you cannot drift along someone's opinion as an object.

mean: in full swing (a campaign or event)
lit: like fire and like the white flowers of reeds

story.text: At the meeting of the states at Huangchi, King Fuchai of Wu, contending with Jin for leadership, drew up his troops in great square formations during the night. The central army was all in white, with white banners, white armour and white-feathered arrows, and looked like a field of white reed flowers; the left army was all in red and looked like fire; the right was all in black. The display was meant to overawe Jin.

use.how: Adverbial or predicate, typically 正在如火如荼地进行 / 开展: describes a large campaign, contest or season of events at its height.

near.diff: 热火朝天 paints a visible scene of people busily working; 如火如荼 says a large-scale campaign or event is at its height, mostly in writing.

cue: A news report says the city's month-long book fair, with events in every district, is now at its peak. How does the report describe it?

ctx.s: 世界杯正在{如火如荼}地进行。
ctx.en: The World Cup is now in full swing.

ctx.s: 眼下，全市的植树活动开展得{如火如荼}。
ctx.en: At the moment the city-wide tree-planting campaign is in full swing.

ctx.s: 今年的读书节已进入第三周，各区的活动{如火如荼}。
ctx.en: This year's reading festival is in its third week, and events across the districts are at their height.

ctx.s: 在招聘季{如火如荼}的时候，很多学生一天要参加好几场面试。
ctx.en: When the recruitment season is at its peak, many students sit several interviews a day.

ctx.s: 全国人口普查工作目前正{如火如荼}地开展。
ctx.en: The national census is currently in full swing.

ctx.s: 新能源汽车的价格战打得{如火如荼}，消费者成了最大的赢家。
ctx.en: The price war over new-energy cars is raging, and consumers are the biggest winners.

bad.s: 今天三十八度，天气{如火如荼}。
bad.en: (meant: it's thirty-eight degrees, scorching hot today)
bad.why: Despite the fire in it, it never describes hot weather; it describes a campaign or event in full swing.

bad.s: 我一个人在家{如火如荼}地写作业。
bad.en: (meant: I'm at home busily doing my homework)
bad.why: It describes a large collective campaign or event, not one person's small task.

lit: hot fire leaping toward the sky

use.how: Complement or attributive: 干得热火朝天, 热火朝天的工地. Describes a lively scene of many people working or busy with enthusiasm.

near.diff: 如火如荼 is mostly written and says a campaign or event is at its height; 热火朝天 paints the visible bustle of people busily at work.

cue: On the day before the school fair, the hall is full of parents and pupils hammering, painting and shouting to each other. How do you describe the scene?

ctx.s: 工地上大家干得{热火朝天}。
ctx.en: On the building site everyone is working away flat out.

ctx.s: 厨房里{热火朝天}，全家人在一起包饺子。
ctx.en: The kitchen is bustling: the whole family is making dumplings together.

ctx.s: “你们在忙什么呢？”“布置晚会的会场，正干得{热火朝天}。”
ctx.en: "What are you all so busy with?" "Setting up the hall for the party; we're right in the thick of it."

ctx.s: 秋收时节，田里到处是{热火朝天}的景象。
ctx.en: At harvest time, the fields are full of busy, lively scenes.

ctx.s: 一进办公室，就看见大家在{热火朝天}地讨论新方案。
ctx.en: As soon as I walked into the office, I saw everyone eagerly debating the new plan.

ctx.s: 比赛前一天，体育馆里彩排得{热火朝天}，没人顾得上吃饭。
ctx.en: The day before the event, the rehearsal in the gym was in full swing and no one had time to eat.

bad.s: 今天{热火朝天}，我们别出门了。
bad.en: (meant: it's boiling hot today, let's stay in)
bad.why: It describes a lively scene of busy activity, not hot weather.

bad.s: 他一个人坐在图书馆里{热火朝天}地看书。
bad.en: (meant: he sat alone in the library reading intently)
bad.why: It paints noisy, bustling activity, usually of a group; quiet solitary study does not fit.

lit: a big broadsword and a wide axe

use.how: Adverbial with 地, or predicate: 大刀阔斧地改革 / 裁员 / 删改. Describes decisive, large-scale changes or cuts.

near.diff: 雷厉风行 stresses speed and strictness in carrying out orders; 大刀阔斧 stresses the boldness and scale of the changes made.

cue: A new director arrives at a loss-making firm, closes three departments, scraps half the products and rewrites the rules within a year. How did she reform it?

ctx.s: 新校长上任后{大刀阔斧}地进行改革。
ctx.en: After taking office, the new head carried out bold, sweeping reforms.

ctx.s: 这篇稿子太长，编辑{大刀阔斧}地删掉了一半。
ctx.en: The draft was too long, so the editor boldly cut half of it.

ctx.s: “这么大的问题，慢慢改行吗？”“不行，必须{大刀阔斧}地改。”
ctx.en: "With a problem this big, can we change things gradually?" "No, we have to make bold, sweeping changes."

ctx.s: 面对连年亏损，公司{大刀阔斧}地砍掉了一半产品线。
ctx.en: Facing years of losses, the company made sweeping cuts and dropped half its product lines.

ctx.s: 他做事{大刀阔斧}，不过细节上有时考虑得不够。
ctx.en: He acts boldly and on a large scale, though he sometimes doesn't think through the details.

ctx.s: 这次改造{大刀阔斧}，老街几乎换了一副面貌。
ctx.en: The renovation was sweeping, and the old street looks almost completely different.

bad.s: 他{大刀阔斧}地改了文章里的一个错别字。
bad.en: (meant: he fixed one typo in the article)
bad.why: It describes bold, large-scale changes; correcting one small error is the opposite.

bad.s: 他{大刀阔斧}地骂了我一顿。
bad.en: (meant: he gave me a fierce telling-off)
bad.why: It is about decisive reforms or cuts, not about harsh or violent words.

mean: to go by the facts, realistic
lit: from real things, seek what is right

story.text: Liu De, Prince Xian of Hejian and a son of Emperor Jing of Han, loved learning and old books. When he obtained a good text from the common people, he had a fine copy made and gave it to the owner, keeping the original for himself, so his collection grew to rival the court's. The history of the Han sums him up as one who studied, loved antiquity, and sought what was right from real evidence.

use.how: Predicate, adverbial (实事求是地说 / 评价) or attributive (实事求是的态度): judging or reporting according to the facts, without exaggeration.

near.diff: 脚踏实地 praises working steadily and diligently; 实事求是 is about judging and speaking according to the facts.

cue: Asked whether the project will finish on time, an engineer neither promises the impossible nor panics, but lays out exactly what has been done and what remains. What attitude is she showing?

ctx.s: {实事求是}地说，这次我们做得不够好。
ctx.en: To be honest about it, we didn't do well enough this time.

ctx.s: 写报告要{实事求是}，不能夸大成绩。
ctx.en: A report has to stick to the facts; you mustn't exaggerate the results.

ctx.s: “你觉得他能当选吗？”“{实事求是}地讲，希望不大。”
ctx.en: "Do you think he'll be elected?" "Realistically speaking, his chances aren't good."

ctx.s: 医生{实事求是}地把病情告诉了病人，没有隐瞒。
ctx.en: The doctor told the patient plainly how things stood, hiding nothing.

ctx.s: 评价一个人要{实事求是}，既看到优点，也看到缺点。
ctx.en: When you assess someone you have to go by the facts, seeing both strengths and weaknesses.

ctx.s: 这位记者{实事求是}的报道态度赢得了读者的信任。
ctx.en: The reporter's commitment to sticking to the facts won the readers' trust.

bad.s: 他每天都{实事求是}地工作，从不偷懒。
bad.en: (meant: he works steadily every day and never slacks)
bad.why: It is about judging and speaking according to the facts, not about working steadily and diligently.

bad.s: 我们要{实事求是}这个问题。
bad.en: (meant: we should look at this problem realistically)
bad.why: It takes no object; introduce the problem with a preposition first, or use the idiom adverbially before a verb like 'look at'.

lit: to judge all things by one measure

use.how: Almost always negated: 不能 / 不可 / 很难一概而论. Says cases differ and must not be judged by one general rule.

near.diff: 因人而异 states that something varies from person to person; 一概而论 warns against judging different cases as if they were the same.

cue: Someone says that all online courses are useless. You think some are excellent and some are poor, so a blanket verdict is unfair. What do you reply?

ctx.s: 网课好不好，不能{一概而论}。
ctx.en: Whether online courses are good or not depends; you can't make a blanket judgement.

ctx.s: 每个孩子情况不同，这种事很难{一概而论}。
ctx.en: Every child is different, so it's hard to generalise about this.

ctx.s: “年轻人是不是都不爱读书？”“这可不能{一概而论}。”
ctx.en: "Is it true that young people don't like reading?" "You really can't lump them all together."

ctx.s: 同样是加班，有的出于自愿，有的出于无奈，不可{一概而论}。
ctx.en: Overtime is not all the same: some people choose it and some have no choice, so it can't be judged as one thing.

ctx.s: 有人一提到网红就说是骗子，这种{一概而论}的看法并不客观。
ctx.en: Some people call every influencer a fraud; that kind of sweeping view isn't objective.

ctx.s: 转基因食品是否安全，专家们认为要具体分析，不宜{一概而论}。
ctx.en: On whether GM foods are safe, experts say each case needs analysing and a blanket judgement is unwise.

bad.s: 他{一概而论}地拒绝了所有的邀请。
bad.en: (meant: he turned down every invitation without exception)
bad.why: It means judging different cases as if they were the same, not doing something to all of them; only its first two characters mean 'without exception'.

bad.s: 这本书{一概而论}了中国历史。
bad.en: (meant: this book summarises Chinese history)
bad.why: It does not mean 'to summarise'; it means wrongly treating different cases as one, and it is usually negated.

mean: to adapt measures to local conditions
lit: according to the land, devise what is suitable

story.text: When Helü became king of Wu, he asked Wu Zixu how to make the state secure and powerful. Wu Zixu advised him to build city walls, set up defences, fill the granaries and stock the armoury. In the exchange that follows, the walls and storehouses are to be built to suit the lie of the land, which is where the phrase comes from.

use.how: Predicate or adverbial (因地制宜地发展): fitting plans, farming, building or policy to the conditions of a particular place.

near.diff: 因材施教 fits teaching to each student; 因地制宜 fits plans and measures to the conditions of a place.
入乡随俗 is a person adopting local customs; 因地制宜 is designing measures to suit local conditions.

cue: Planners in a dry northern county grow drought-hardy crops while a wet southern county plants rice, instead of copying one national plan. What principle are they following?

ctx.s: 种什么庄稼，要{因地制宜}。
ctx.en: Which crops to grow depends on the local conditions.

ctx.s: 山区缺水，当地{因地制宜}，发展了果树种植。
ctx.en: The mountain area is short of water, so the locals adapted to it and took up fruit growing.

ctx.s: “别的城市的经验能直接照搬吗？”“不行，还得{因地制宜}。”
ctx.en: "Can we just copy other cities' experience?" "No, we still have to adapt it to our own conditions."

ctx.s: 这家连锁店在各地{因地制宜}，菜单都有当地特色。
ctx.en: The chain adapts to each place, and every menu has local touches.

ctx.s: 老房子改造没有统一模板，只能{因地制宜}地设计。
ctx.en: There's no standard template for renovating old houses; each design has to suit the site.

ctx.s: 各省应当{因地制宜}，制定适合本地的发展计划。
ctx.en: Each province should adapt to its own conditions and draw up a development plan that suits it.

bad.s: 王老师对每个学生都{因地制宜}，教法各不相同。
bad.en: (meant: Ms Wang teaches each student in a way that suits them)
bad.why: It is about adapting measures to the conditions of a place; teaching suited to each student calls for a different idiom.

bad.s: 他到了北京就{因地制宜}，学会了说北京话。
bad.en: (meant: in Beijing he fitted in and picked up the local accent)
bad.why: It is about planning measures to suit a place, not about a person adopting local customs or speech.

use.how: Predicate whose subject is a thing (效果、感受、方法): 效果因人而异. States that it depends on the individual.

near.diff: 一概而论 is judging all cases as one, usually negated; 因人而异 simply states that something varies by person.
因材施教 is the act of teaching each student differently; 因人而异 just observes that something differs by person.

cue: A friend asks whether a new sleep app will work for them. It helped you but did nothing for your sister. What do you say about its effect?

ctx.s: 这种药的效果{因人而异}。
ctx.en: How well this medicine works varies from person to person.

ctx.s: “学会游泳要多久？”“这个{因人而异}，有人一周，有人一个月。”
ctx.en: "How long does it take to learn to swim?" "It depends on the person: some take a week, some a month."

ctx.s: 对同一部电影的感受{因人而异}，不必强求一致。
ctx.en: People react differently to the same film; there's no need to insist everyone agree.

ctx.s: 减肥的方法{因人而异}，适合别人的不一定适合你。
ctx.en: Ways of losing weight differ by person; what suits others won't necessarily suit you.

ctx.s: 每天需要睡几个小时，其实{因人而异}。
ctx.en: How many hours of sleep you need each day actually varies from person to person.

ctx.s: 这里的奖金分配{因人而异}，主要看每个人的工作量。
ctx.en: Bonuses here differ from person to person, depending mainly on each one's workload.

bad.s: 他这个人很{因人而异}，你永远猜不透他。
bad.en: (meant: he is unpredictable; you can never figure him out)
bad.why: It describes how a thing varies across people, not a person's character, and it cannot be modified by 'very'.

bad.s: 我和我哥哥{因人而异}，性格完全不同。
bad.en: (meant: my brother and I are completely different in character)
bad.why: Its subject is a thing that varies by person, not the people being compared; it cannot mean 'we are different'.

mean: to learn from others' strengths to fix one's weaknesses
lit: take from the long to make up the short

use.how: Predicate, often with 互相 or 相互: two people or groups learn from each other's strengths. 大家互相取长补短。

near.diff: 扬长避短 is making the most of your own strengths and steering around your weak points; 取长补短 is learning from others' strengths to fix your weak points.
集思广益 gathers many people's ideas to solve one problem; 取长补短 is learning from each other to improve oneself.

cue: One teammate is great at design but weak at coding; the other is the reverse. They sit together every week to teach each other. What are they doing?

ctx.s: 同学之间要互相学习，{取长补短}。
ctx.en: Classmates should learn from each other, each making up for their weak points with the other's strengths.

ctx.s: 他们俩一个擅长设计，一个擅长编程，正好{取长补短}。
ctx.en: One of them is good at design and the other at coding, so they complement each other perfectly.

ctx.s: “为什么要和别的学校交流？”“为了{取长补短}，提高自己。”
ctx.en: "Why do exchanges with other schools?" "To learn from their strengths and improve ourselves."

ctx.s: 两家公司合作以后{取长补短}，产品质量明显提高了。
ctx.en: Once the two companies started working together they learned from each other, and product quality clearly improved.

ctx.s: 中西医如果能{取长补短}，对病人会更有好处。
ctx.en: If Chinese and Western medicine could learn from each other's strengths, patients would benefit more.

ctx.s: 新老员工在一起工作，可以相互{取长补短}。
ctx.en: When new and experienced staff work together, they can each learn from the other's strengths.

bad.s: 面试时要{取长补短}，多谈优点，少谈缺点。
bad.en: (meant: in an interview, talk up your strengths and avoid your weak points)
bad.why: It means learning from others' strengths, not presenting your own strengths and hiding your weak points.

bad.s: 这条裤子太长了，裁缝帮我{取长补短}。
bad.en: (meant: the trousers were too long, so the tailor altered them)
bad.why: It is never used literally for cutting or altering things; it means learning from others' strengths.
